message.content:
I don’t have live access to current air‑quality data, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment. However, here’s what you can do to get up‑to‑date information:

| Source | How to use it | What you’ll see |
|--------|---------------|-----------------|
| **AirNow (EPA)** | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. | Current AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), forecast for the next 48 h. |
| **Weather apps** | Many weather apps (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, Apple Weather) include an “Air Quality” tab. | Real‑time AQI, health advisories, and trend graphs. |
| **Local news sites** | Check the LA Times or local TV station websites; they often post daily air‑quality summaries. | Narrative reports on smog levels, traffic‑related pollution, and any alerts. |
| **Mobile apps** | Apps like Plume Labs’ Air Report or BreezoMeter give push notifications for high‑pollution days. | Alerts, health recommendations, and historical data. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities, the EPA’s AirNow site also offers a “Health Recommendations” section that tells you whether it’s safe to exercise, how long you should limit exposure, and whether people with asthma or heart conditions should stay indoors.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like a quick summary of what typical Los Angeles air‑quality looks like during different seasons!
